newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SPH expects flat growth for FY1997.
newsitem.headline: SPH expects flat growth for FY1997.

text.p: Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) said on Friday it expects flat earnings growth for the financial year ending August 31 1997.
"It depends on the economy. If the economy maintains here, I think we should have about the same returns," chairman Lim Kim San told a press conference.
He said although news print prices had stablised to about US$650 per tonne, much lower than last year, wage costs had gone up.
He said the group's new presses which would be operational by January 1997, would yield more colour advertisements and might improve advertising revenue.
He said the group's results for fiscal year 1996 were mainly impacted by Singpore's slower economic growth.
SPH's advertising revenue grew at a slower rate of 6.9 percent for fiscal year 1996 and growth was slower than the first half. He added advertising growth would depend on Singapore's economic growth.
He said the group's newspaper circulation grew by 1.7 percent for fiscal year 1996: "As far as newspaper circulation is concern we have reached maturity."

Lim said the group's multimedia business was key to its future growth but he did not expect substantial contributions to earnings from this segment until the year 2000. He added the group had invested in properties and other investments and future earnings would be impacted by these.

He said there were plans to develop the site of Times House, one of its offices in central Singapore, in three to four years time. There were no fixed plans yet but the site had been re-zoned by the government for housing development.
